accuracy.evidence: Checked against the National Curriculum spoken language statements (articulate and justify answers, arguments and opinions; take part in discussions, role play and debates), Development Matters 2021 (3-4: express a point of view and debate when they disagree; Reception: connect one idea to another using connectives) and Common Core W.K.1 (state an opinion or preference) and W.1.1 (supply a reason and a sense of closure). The lab's final talk step models exactly that W.1.1 shape: opinion, reasons, closing So line.

misconceptions.evidence: Each wrong card is a documented early-years slip: the circular reason (because I just do, because it is), the true but off-topic reason (it is Tuesday, I had toast), the vague evaluative reason (it is good, it is nice), restating the opinion as its own reason (it is football), attacking the speaker (You are wrong!) and the belief that when two children disagree one must be wrong.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagopine is a speech-bubble builder: phrase cards are dragged into a bubble in speaking order (I think, opinion, because-reason; then a four-part talk with and and So), and the pick steps judge the reason against the opinion in the bubble. flagreason (speaker's reasons, 9-11) and flagfvo (fact vs opinion) analyse given text; none builds a spoken justification. The shingle gate passed.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the order rule by trying it: dropping because they play with me first says Say what you think first, and the bubble only reads aloud once the frame is complete. Picking I just do or it is Tuesday triggers a reason that names why it fails, so the child works out what a reason must do before the step text confirms it.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: Yes for is because I just do a reason (children often accept it), because it is good as the more helpful reason, and Yes, one is wrong for Mia and Ben disagreeing about rain. The task straight after tests each guess and the done message names whether it held.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Four rotating questions with eight tagged wrong answers, each naming its slip: no reason given, circular I just do, vague it is good, off-topic red hat, unkind you are wrong, polite but reasonless disagreement, and confusing because with and then or the end.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores FK 1.3 against the family limit of 5.0, with short sentences and a worked example in each paragraph. Adult text scores FK 7.7 against 10 and uses the curriculum terms opinion, reason, justify, articulate, point of view, connective, conjunction, sentence stem, agree and disagree, and sense of closure.

no_filler.evidence: No stock phrases; the filler gate passed. Every kid paragraph gives a rule plus an example sentence, every adult paragraph carries either curriculum, the sentence-stem method, named mistakes or what the lab does. The explanation overlaps other lessons by less than 12 percent.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark (steps 1, 4 and 5) show the bubble, a 46 px high full-width card per answer and wrapped text with nothing clipped; the four-card talk step fits by shrinking the bubble. A real pointer drag on the iPhone viewport dropped I think into the bubble, gave the out-of-order message for the because card, then completed the sentence.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs axe run found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme on desktop or iPhone, and no console errors. Every card on the canvas is also a labelled button below it (Next part or Choose plus the card text), and the canvas aria-label reads each result or correction aloud.

sources: DfE (2013) English programmes of study KS1-2: spoken language statements
DfE (2021) Development Matters: communication and language (3-4 year olds and Reception)
Common Core State Standards ELA W.K.1, W.1.1
